evidence: FR-001 requires a documented manual command and prerequisites; FR-016 assigns contextual analysis to an agent skill and discovery and safe updates to a local helper.
FR-003 and FR-019 define whole-session selection and require uncertainty about closure, workspace, completeness, or activity time to be surfaced.

Frozen design.md, Builder choices to resolve in planning, explicitly delegates executable packaging, source adapters, closure evidence, identifiers, and model/runtime selection. No unsupported host API assumptions or additional interface blockers were identified.

FR-009 requires preservation of human edits and detection or prevention of concurrent-update conflicts; User Story 2, Scenario 4 permits retaining the edit or reporting a conflict without overwriting it.
FR-012, FR-014, and FR-019 require distinguishable incomplete or failed outcomes and preservation of the existing backlog before a safe update.

Edge Cases explicitly covers interrupted runs, changing or partially read sources, overlapping windows, and uncertain session metadata; locking or optimistic concurrency is explicitly delegated to planning.
FR-004 requires reliable association with a configurable root; Edge Cases excludes similarly prefixed outside-root paths and uncertain metadata from assumed eligibility.
FR-013 prohibits secret disclosure in the shared file, console, and intermediate artifacts, and requires treating transcripts as data rather than instructions.

FR-018 prohibits modification of audited skills, completion marking, external issue creation, commits, pushes, and deployment; SC-007 requires representative secret and instruction-like transcript tests.
FR-006 requires stable issue identifiers and evidence identifying source, session, and occurrence.
FR-012 requires reporting the fixed window, source coverage, skipped or uncertain sessions, read and analysis failures, and backlog result, distinguishing full, partial, and failed runs.
User Story 3, Scenario 2 requires actionable, distinguishable outcomes for missing prerequisites or incomplete coverage; FR-017 requires non-interactive repeatability without enabling a schedule.
FR-001 and SC-006 require documented prerequisites and verification of actual manual invocation in a representative environment.
FR-017 prohibits installing or enabling a schedule; the approved design selects a skill plus local helper rather than requiring a separately published standalone binary.

Frozen design.md explicitly delegates executable and skill packaging to planning and requires host-format compatibility to be verified or reported as a limitation. A public release pipeline or broader platform matrix is not an approved-scope requirement.
FR-002 captures one audit-start instant; FR-006 through FR-008 require stable identifiers, one shared backlog, and individually traceable grouped occurrences.
FR-009 and FR-014 protect human-maintained content; FR-015 requires idempotence over identical evidence and identifiable duplicate or split representations.
FR-010 requires evidence linking subsequent recurrence to a completed fix; Edge Cases explicitly prohibits asserting a regression when post-fix timing cannot be established.
Key Entities defines runs, sessions, evidence occurrences, issues, and linked regressions. Identifier mechanisms and the issue-file representation are explicitly delegated to planning.

SC-001 through SC-007 cover eligibility, finding fields, repeat-run deduplication, regression and concurrent-edit preservation, source limitations, manual invocation, secrets, and transcript instructions.
User Scenarios & Testing and Edge Cases cover whole-session context, ambiguous metadata, interrupted runs, duplicate representations, and incomplete coverage.

FR-005 requires contextual identification and exclusion of unrelated problems, but SC-002 only constrains "Every reported fixture finding"; no measurable outcome explicitly requires recovering known supported problems and rejecting unrelated controls.
Exact test fixtures are delegated to planning in frozen design.md; ARCH-001 requests behavioral acceptance assertions, not a fixture framework or model choice.

findings.completion_criterion: Add a measurable analysis acceptance criterion requiring representative Hermes and Codex cases with known supported skill friction to produce the expected problems with supporting context, and unrelated-problem controls to produce no unrelated issues. Verify that an analyzer returning no findings fails the positive cases and an analyzer reporting unrelated project problems fails the controls. Leave fixture design, semantic matching, and runtime selection to planning.
evidence: spec.md, Functional Requirements, FR-005: "The system MUST identify friction relevant to using or attempting to use `refine-idea` or `implement-refine-idea`, including user corrections, observed failures, and extra setup; unrelated project problems MUST NOT be included solely because they appeared in an eligible session."

spec.md, Measurable Outcomes, SC-001: "all eligible sessions are selected and all open, outside-root, and outside-window sessions are excluded." This establishes selection correctness, not analysis correctness.

spec.md, Measurable Outcomes, SC-002: "Every reported fixture finding contains an affected skill, actionable proposed improvement, priority, `Not Fixed` initial status, and traceable session evidence." This checks reported findings without requiring expected findings to be reported.

spec.md, User Story 1, Acceptance Scenario 2 conditions recording on "When the auditor confirms a functional improvement is supported by context" rather than explicitly requiring detection of a known supported improvement.
findings.summary: The measurable outcomes test discovery and finding format but do not require the contextual analyzer to detect known, evidence-backed friction or reject unrelated problems. An analyzer that misses the seeded problems could satisfy the stated format checks, leaving the feature's central behavior without a measurable acceptance gate. Fixture construction and model selection remain builder-owned; the gap is the required behavioral assertion.
